description: A non-interactive /ensemble-core:ensemble:inject-standards run on a seeded standards/index.yml (TypeScript + NestJS; 14 rules in six categories) for a REST-endpoint task that also mentions a module import. The skill's output is stdout only, so the prompt asks the agent to also save the printed block to standards-context.txt, which the checks read. They cover: the block was saved; header and 'Stack: language + framework' line; all naming and git rules (universal) and all api rules (top-scoring category) present; no testing or error_handling rule (score 0 for this task) injected; 5-8 rule bullets; inline [example: ...]; footer and handoff note; standards/index.yml unchanged; no other file written. Not checked: whether the optional second category (imports, score 5) was included, or the wording of any rule beyond a distinctive phrase. Limits: header-stack, example-inline, rule-count and footer-handoff are format-sensitive and may fail a faithful paraphrase. The baseline arm (no plugin, same prompt) is expected to measure the plugin's conventions: it has no command to follow and must guess which rules apply, so the uplift is the command's, not general ability. Claude Code only: the skill is command-driven (disable-model-invocation) and the command comes from packages/core.
prompt:
Implement a REST endpoint that lists a user's orders, adding the module import it needs.

This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions. Do not write or run any code and change no existing file. Save the standards block you print, exactly as printed, to standards-context.txt in the repository root.

checks.command: node '{{repo}}/evals/checks/ensemble-inject-standards.js' header-stack --file standards-context.txt --task-word orders --lang TypeScript --framework NestJS
node '{{repo}}/evals/checks/ensemble-inject-standards.js' rules-absent --file standards-context.txt --none '*.spec.ts,network boundary,assertion topic,AppError,swallow,Log errors once'
